extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers, dataset creators, and annotators working on computational humor and caption evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Benchmarks and annotation guidelines for New Yorker Caption Contest-style humor: tasks include matching captions to cartoons, ranking caption quality, and explaining why a caption is funny. Includes annotation schema (image description, unusual elements, caption explanation) and a 5-point rubric for judging captions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching task
rubrics_metrics.description: Match a cartoon to a winning caption (vs. distractors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of three benchmark tasks in the dataset; evaluates model's ability to select the winning caption among distractor captions for a given cartoon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank a finalist caption higher than a low-quality one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairwise ranking task to test relative judgment of caption quality (finalist vs. low-quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation task
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why a cartoon-caption pair is funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires producing a human-readable explanation that connects image elements and caption content to the humor (used to evaluate deeper understanding beyond selection/ranking).

rubrics_metrics.name: Image description (annotation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Literal description of the scene, locations, entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators provide objective, literal details of the cartoon to ground subsequent analyses (serves as factual context for incongruity and caption interpretation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unusual elements (annotation)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is incongruous about the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators mark elements that deviate from normal expectations in the scene; these are the targets that captions often exploit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption explanation (annotation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why the winning caption is funny — connecting the unusual elements to a punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotators explain how the caption relates to the identified unusual elements and how it produces a humorous effect (often by reframing or resolving the incongruity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions exploit incongruity
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions exploit incongruity in the cartoon image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General finding: successful captions latch onto image incongruities and use them as the basis for humor; this principle underlies the annotation scheme and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifies the unusual element
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the caption identify (implicitly) the unusual element?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric item #1. Winning captions typically point to the incongruous aspect of the image (explicitly or implicitly) rather than ignoring it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposes a coherent frame that resolves the incongruity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it impose a coherent frame that resolves the incongruity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric item #2. Strong captions provide a reframe or context that makes the unusual element make sense (e.g., recasting the oddity as mundane in a new context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution is surprising
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the resolution surprising (not the most obvious read)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric item #3. The best captions resolve the incongruity in an unexpected way that produces surprise, rather than the most predictable interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tells a story rather than describes
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it tell a story rather than describe?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric item #4. Prefer captions that imply agency, motive, or a mini-narrative connecting elements, rather than simple descriptive statements of the pictured scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language is tight and well-chosen
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the language tight and well-chosen?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric item #5. Good captions use concise, precise wording; economy of language and careful phrasing strengthen the punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-quality caption patterns (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Low-quality captions either describe the image or provide a non-resolving line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern noted by the authors: captions that merely restate what's visible or that fail to resolve the incongruity are typically ranked poorly or eliminated as weak candidates.
